knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A premium rests on a benefit the client receives and can describe. A brand name the client has never heard explained, or a comparison claim, gives the client nothing to check.
The correct statement names the audience, a checkable change, a method and a deliverable. The cure claim is a health claim and the ancient-method claim is not checkable.

Accurate description of what has been studied, with no implied lineage or endorsement, is the appropriate step. Using a tradition's name as a title misrepresents the offer, and declining to write a position leaves staff with no shared answer.

practicalCriteria: Candidate writes a value statement with an audience, a checkable change, a method and a deliverable. The assessor confirms each element is present and that it matches the class plan.
Candidate removes or reworks every health or treatment claim in the draft. The assessor confirms none remain on the sample channels.
Candidate writes an attribution position for one practice. The assessor confirms it avoids implied lineage, credentials or endorsement.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Value statement, saved with its date
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: A cure, treatment or guaranteed health outcome is about to be published
A sacred or religious term is about to be used as a marketing name
A client has been told of a lineage, certificate or endorsement that the business cannot evidence
